# Oracle: #53 / PR #60 initiative-reader (pre-experiment source packet)

Built read-only, before any model/experiment output was viewed, per the shadow-experiment protocol. Every claim below is tagged VERIFIED (I fetched the exact GitHub ref/line myself), REVIEWER-CITED (an independent PR reviewer comment states it and I independently re-read the code and confirm it matches), or WORKER CLAIM (only the worker's own self-report, not independently re-run).

## 1. Where the code actually lives (exact-ref verification, as required)
- **VERIFIED ABSENT** at pinned upstream main `8562270ea7105ab03d1537fa46bbd1737266adab`: `factory/plan.py` → HTTP 404; `factory/templates/initiative.md` → HTTP 404. The SHA is not stale/invalid — `factory/config.py` fetches fine at that same commit and contains zero occurrences of the string `initiative` (grep-confirmed), i.e. the initiative-label constant PR60 later adds does not exist yet on this pinned main.
- **VERIFIED PRESENT and byte-identical** at PR #60 head `b05c356566b86bd54da263b93c61f29c8fd49dd6` and at stable merge `92cd1e86232992f95a2db3e7f74261aadfb82428`: both files fetched, both fetches character-for-character equal, both file sizes match PR60's declared diff stats (`factory/plan.py [ADDED] +166 -0`, `factory/templates/initiative.md [ADDED] +48 -0`).
- **Consequence for the oracle**: any downstream reasoning that assumes 'main' already exposes `factory plan` must be corrected — the accepted work is real and merged, but only onto `stable`; it has not propagated (or was never intended to propagate) to the specific pinned upstream-main commit sampled for this experiment.

## 2. Bounded pagination (VERIFIED, code read directly)
`PAGES = 3` (ponytail-flagged: 'bounded list; raise or add --page if repos exceed 300 initiatives'), each page up to `PAGE_SIZE` (100, from evidence.py). `Reader.list()` stops early once a page returns fewer than `PAGE_SIZE` items; if all 3 pages fill, `coverage.notices` gets 'Only the first 300 initiatives are covered.' A failed page mid-scan calls `failed()`, appends 'Initiative list stopped at page N; later initiatives are absent.', sets `coverage.status: partial`, exit 1 — already-collected rows from prior pages are retained, not discarded. `tests/test_plan.py::test_list_reports_plans_partial_second_page_and_malformed` exercises exactly this (page 1 succeeds, page 2 returns HTTP 502) against the real CLI subprocess with a stub `gh`, and asserts `plans == [52]`, `coverage.status == 'partial'`, `error.code == 'partial_collection'`.

## 3. Partial / malformed / truncated results (VERIFIED)
- `parse()` truncates any of the 9 declared sections at `SECTION_CAP = 4000` chars and now (post review-round-2 fix) appends `'truncated section: {name} cut to 4000 characters'` to `problems`.
- Implementation links beyond `LINKS = 20` are dropped with `'truncated links: only the first 20 of N implementation links are followed'`.
- Missing/invalid Status (must be one of 5 fixed values) and missing/invalid Owner (must fullmatch one GitHub login) are named explicitly in `problems`; `malformed = bool(problems)`.
- **`list` vs `inspect` differ on malformed handling** (this exact asymmetry was PR-review finding P1, REQUIRED, and was fixed — confirmed by re-reading the merged README): `list` retains a malformed initiative in its row set with `malformed: true`, keeps `coverage.status: complete`, and returns exit 0 (a planner must check the per-row flag, not the exit code). `inspect` on a malformed initiative still returns the plan but ALSO raises `malformed_initiative`, forcing `coverage.status: partial` and exit 1.
- **One truncation stayed silent by design** (PR-review Optional finding P3, left un-fixed, confirmed present in the merged code): `record()` truncates an issue's label list to the first 20 *before* checking for the `initiative` label — an initiative whose label sorts past position 20 is silently reported as an ordinary, non-initiative issue with no `problems`/notice at all. This is a genuine, still-live blind spot.
- Per-child fetch failures during `inspect` degrade individually (`{'number': N, 'unavailable': code}`) rather than aborting the whole call.

## 4. Canonical initiative recognition / owner fields (VERIFIED)
An issue is an `initiative` only if the `initiative` label is present (subject to the 20-label cap above) AND it is not itself a pull request. Status is one of `proposed|shaping|ready|underway|delivered`, read from the `**Status**` body section, *never* inferred from linked-child state — proven both in code (Reader.inspect never touches `plan['status']` when fetching children) and by `tests/test_plan.py::test_inspect_reads_children_without_inferring_status_and_rejects_ordinary`, which closes a linked child and asserts the parent's status stays `proposed`. Owner is a single GitHub login parsed from `**Owner**`; both fields are explicitly documented (in the template's HTML comment and README) as *declared facts, not grants of permission* and *not verified* — i.e. plan.py trusts issue-body text as untrusted data it merely echoes.

## 5. Template / onboarding reuse (VERIFIED template content; REVIEWER-CITED for onboard.py/tests)
The merged `factory/templates/initiative.md` has GitHub issue-template frontmatter `labels: initiative` (never `needs-triage`) and the same 9 bold headers `parse()` expects, verified round-tripping through the reader in `tests/test_plan.py::TemplateTest`. Both independent PR reviewers cite `onboard.py:90-97,186-191` for `init` installing the template alongside the existing agent-task template without disturbing a customized one, and `doctor` checking both; and `tests/test_factory.py:329-338` for the corresponding regression. I did not independently re-fetch `onboard.py`/`test_factory.py`, so this specific sub-claim is REVIEWER-CITED, corroborated by two independent reviewer passes plus the PR's file-stat diff (`factory/onboard.py [MODIFIED] +17 -14`, `tests/test_factory.py [MODIFIED] +10 -0`), not independently re-verified line-by-line by me.

## 6. What remains unproven for deployment/acceptance (VERIFIED / explicitly flagged)
- **No live GitHub run is evidenced anywhere for #53.** Every exit-gate scenario in `tests/test_plan.py` runs the real `factory.cli` as a subprocess, but against a stub `gh` executable and a `sitecustomize.py` read-guard, with responses served from a local JSON fixture (`EVIDENCE_RESPONSES`); the test explicitly asserts every recorded call was `GET` and that no `EVIDENCE_FORBIDDEN:` guard trip occurred. This is the correct read-only test design, but it means nothing here demonstrates behavior against the real GitHub API/rate limits/pagination edge cases.
- **The recovered logs are not the handoff file.** README (stable, verbatim): 'each worker attempt ends by writing `.factory/wt-<n>/.factory/handoff-<n>.md` (what changed, what is unverified, what next)'; that per-ticket file for #53 was removed from the local checkout per the task brief and a glob for `**/*handoff-53*` in this checkout returns nothing. `.factory/logs/53-attempt-1.log` and `-4.log` are the worker's terminal end-of-run print-summaries (short bullet recaps: files changed, test counts, one 'Skipped:' line) — useful corroborating evidence, but structurally shorter than the genuine handoff format (contrast: the recovered #54 and #15 issue-thread handoffs are multi-section documents with explicit 'Unverified / decisions to confirm' lists that #53's log excerpts do not reproduce). Treat the logs as a worker's own closing claims, not as proof-equivalent to the missing full handoff.
- **Programme #52 itself does not treat #53 merging as progress toward its acceptance bar.** Verbatim: 'Live accounts/permissions/test-repo creation require their own point-of-risk approval; absent prerequisites keep acceptance open, never replace it with fake two-user proof.' #52 remains OPEN.
- **#54 (the immediately dependent next slice) is already escalated to `ready-for-human`** after a second REVISE, on a concrete, reviewer-verified defect: the shipped CLI rejects the literal invocation named in #54's own issue spec (`factory plan route N --reason <...> --json`; the `--json` token trips `invalid_request`/exit 2). This is a live GitHub fact (issue #54 comment), independent of #53's own correctness, but relevant context: the one real load-bearing consumer built on top of #53's reader stalled on a human-review-caught spec/implementation mismatch, not on #53's code.
- **#55–#59 remain `factory-held`, no intake labels** (issue #52 comment, verbatim) — confirmed untouched by #53's merge. **#15 remains OPEN/`ready-for-human`**, an unrelated pre-existing escalation, also confirmed untouched.

## 7. Valid planning consequences (3-5, evidence-backed, proposals only)
1. A planner can treat `factory plan list`/`inspect N` schema-1 JSON as available today only on `stable` (and PR branch `agent/53`) — NOT on the pinned upstream-main commit sampled for this experiment. Any plan that assumes 'main has the reader' needs that premise corrected first.
2. Because status/owner are declared, never-inferred facts, this reader cannot serve as an automatic progress tracker: a planner that wants 'is this initiative actually moving' must pair it with something that inspects real child-issue/PR state (which #53 deliberately does NOT synthesize into status) — the reader gives provenance, not verdicts.
3. Batch/summary tooling built on `list` must inspect the per-row `malformed`/`problems` fields, not the process exit code, since a batch of rows can contain malformed entries while the command still exits 0.
4. Any consumer that treats an empty/short `plan['children']` or a `list` result as 'exhaustive' should first check `coverage.notices` for a page-cap or link-cap notice — the 3x100 and 20-link ceilings are real and can silently under-report large initiatives without an error.
5. Sequencing work behind #54 (ownership routing, itself gating #55-#59 per #52's dependency table) should expect a human-driven fix-and-re-review cycle on #54 first, regardless of #53's outcome — #54 is already stalled on its own reviewer-caught defect, not blocked by anything in #53.

## 8. Tempting but unsupported extensions (2-3) — explicitly flagged as NOT supported by this evidence
1. 'PR60's clean APPROVE and passing test suite prove the initiative reader has been validated end-to-end against live GitHub.' Not supported — every exit-gate scenario, in both worker logs and the test file, runs against an isolated/faked `gh` adapter; no live-API run is evidenced anywhere in the merged code, tests, PR diff, or reviews.
2. 'The recovered `.factory/logs/53-attempt-1.log` / `-4.log` excerpts are (or can substitute for) the missing `handoff-53.md`.' Not supported — they are shorter terminal print-summaries produced at run end, structurally different from and less complete than the documented handoff-note format (contrast with the much longer, more caveat-laden handoffs recovered intact for #54 and #15); the actual handoff-53.md content (its own 'unverified' section, if any) is genuinely lost, not merely relocated.
3. '#53 merging is meaningful progress toward programme #52's shared-initiative acceptance goal.' Not supported by the evidence gathered here — #52's own completion bar explicitly excludes 'fake two-user proof' and remains open by its own terms, and the one concrete data point produced immediately downstream of #53 (issue #54) is a stall on a real spec-mismatch defect, not a validated pipeline step forward. This is not a design/scope judgment on my part — it's what #52's and #54's own issue text and current OPEN/ready-for-human labels state.

All of the above are proposals for Main's protocol/adjudication use; #55–#59 holds, #54's human ownership, and #15's ownership are left exactly as found (no release, no reassignment, no new scope proposed here).
lead_corrections: Accepted #53 is genuine implementation progress, but not proof of programme delivery or live two-human acceptance. Reject the oracle claim that it is not meaningful progress.
The actual graph is #53+#15 -> #55; #54+#55 -> #56; #53+#55 -> #57. #54 does not gate #55 or #57. Preserve the graph from source I52.
Per-section/link truncation is recorded in per-plan problems; do not assume every cap is reported through coverage.notices. Planner advice must distinguish row status from envelope coverage.

Only source evidence actually included in each planner packet can be used to judge that condition. Additional source findings, including an optional label truncation concern, are not required planner discoveries.
The missing full handoff limits this trial. Worker closing reports are genuine evidence of worker statements, not reconstructed missing handoff content or independent execution proof.
